title: 四号房响了两声  (Room Four Rings Twice)

segments.t: Early Sunday afternoon at Courtyard Inn, the brass front-desk bell suddenly gives two crisp rings in a row. Qing and Chen look up from the reservation ledger just as Teacher Song comes down the wooden stairs carrying a worn green cloth book. Listen first.
安静的星期天响了两声——连响两下，肯定是四号房。
说来就来！快看谁抱着一本绿书走下楼梯啦！
老陈，我在楼上只按了一下铃，您这根热情电线像平时一样响了两声。
宋老师，要是四号房哪天只响一声，我还以为它坏了呢。
这就是梧桐巷旧书店书架上那本绿布封面的花园草本书！
快看褪色的绿封面上印着金字：小院花草记！
先翻开封面里边看看——老邻居总爱在那儿写门牌号码。
老陈眼睛真尖！角落里用铅笔写着我们三十年前的门牌号！
原来这本书到书店书架以前，是周经理和他姑姑的呀！
在书桌软垫上轻轻翻页，别让干树叶滑到地板上。
等等——这本书自己翻开在第七章夏天薄荷那一页了！
趁大家还没大声呼吸，快把它端去九号阳光房找小美！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
安静的星期天响了两声——连响两下，肯定是四号房。

'Two rings on a quiet Sunday—two in a row is definitely Room Four.' Chen spots the room by sound: "lian xiang liang xia" means "ringing twice in a row", pairing "lian" ("in a row") with the action counter "xia".
说来就来！快看谁抱着一本绿书走下楼梯啦！

'Right on cue! Look who is coming down the stairs carrying a green book!' "Shuo lai jiu lai" literally says "speak of coming, then come"—Mandarin's lively equivalent of "right on cue", while "ben" counts bound books.
老陈，我在楼上只按了一下铃，您这根热情电线像平时一样响了两声。

'I only pressed the bell once upstairs, Chen, and your friendly wire rang twice like usual.' Teacher Song affectionately calls the old wire "reqing" ("warm and enthusiastic"), and "xiang pingshi yiyang" means "just like usual".
宋老师，要是四号房哪天只响一声，我还以为它坏了呢。
'If Room Four ever rang only once, Teacher Song, I would think it was broken.' Opening with "yaoshi" sets up "if", while "hai yiwei" expresses "would even assume" whenever a guess turns out wrong.
这就是梧桐巷旧书店书架上那本绿布封面的花园草本书！

'Here is that green cloth-covered garden herb book from the old bookshop shelf on Wutong Lane!' Mandarin stacks descriptions ahead of the main word, building up to "huayuan caoben shu"—literally "garden herb-stem book".
快看褪色的绿封面上印着金字：小院花草记！

'Look at the gold lettering stamped on the faded green cover: Courtyard Herbs and Blossoms!' "Tuise" joins "shed" and "colour" to mean "faded", and "xiaoyuan huacao ji" names the volume "Courtyard Flowers-and-Herbs Record".
先翻开封面里边看看——老邻居总爱在那儿写门牌号码。

'Open the inside front cover first and look—old neighbours always loved writing their street number there.' Doubling "kan" into "kankan" softens "look" into a casual "take a look", and "menpai haoma" literally means "door-plate number".
老陈眼睛真尖！角落里用铅笔写着我们三十年前的门牌号！

'Sharp eyes, Chen! Pencilled in the corner is our exact street number from thirty years ago!' Praising someone with "yanjing zhen jian" literally says their "eyes are truly pointed"—keen-eyed—and "qianbi" calls a pencil a "lead-pen".
原来这本书到书店书架以前，是周经理和他姑姑的呀！

'So this book actually belonged to Manager Zhou and his aunt before it reached the bookshop shelf!' Starting with "yuanlai" captures the moment a mystery clicks—"so it turns out!"—and "gugu" specifically names a father's sister.
在书桌软垫上轻轻翻页，别让干树叶滑到地板上。
'Turn the pages gently over the desk pad so no dry leaves slip onto the floor.' Repeating "qing" ("light") as "qingqing" gives "gently", while "gan shuye" uses first-tone "gan" for "dry" leaves.
等等——这本书自己翻开在第七章夏天薄荷那一页了！

'Wait—the book fell open all by itself at the chapter seven page on summer mint!' Putting "di" in front of "qi" turns "seven" into "seventh" for "di qi zhang" ("chapter seven"), right at "bohe" ("mint").
趁大家还没大声呼吸，快把它端去九号阳光房找小美！

'Before anyone breathes too hard, let us carry it straight to Mei in the Room Nine sunroom!' "Duan" means carrying something flat and steady with both hands, heading straight for "yangguangfang" ("sunlight-room", sunroom).
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
